tasks.title: Author a restart-safe file-processing queue task
tasks.description:
# Author a restart-safe file-processing queue

## Situation

A small operations team processes locally submitted jobs into result files. A
worker can stop after producing a result but before recording completion. On
restart, the current implementation either repeats the effect or loses the job.
Create a terminal task in which a solver diagnoses and repairs this behavior.

## What you create

Provide a small application, starting source, sample jobs and a documented local
command interface for accepting jobs, processing them, inspecting status and
recovering interrupted work. Choose a suitable language and local persistence
mechanism. Use original data and make the failure reproducible without a network
service or credentials.

The solver must receive a functioning but incorrect application. Do not make the
exercise consist only of filling an empty function or installing a missing tool.

## Behavior the finished task must specify

- Each accepted job has an identifier and immutable input. Repeating the same
  request returns the retained facts. Reusing that identifier for different input
  fails without replacing the original job.
- A completed job has one observable result. Recovery cannot silently duplicate
  its effect or discard a result that was already committed.
- An interrupted job can resume according to a documented recovery rule. Status
  distinguishes unfinished work from a completed result.
- Invalid work does not damage unrelated jobs or erase their history.

You decide the exact formats, command names and commit boundary, and explain them
in `instruction.md`. Define what counts as the job's effect. A useful choice is
publication of a result file plus a durable completion record; make the allowed
state at every interruption point explicit. State whether simultaneous workers
are supported rather than leaving the solver to guess.

## Evidence the task must support

Verification should stop execution at a controlled boundary, restart using the
same retained state and inspect both job records and output files. Avoid relying
only on a timing-sensitive sleep. Include a sequence with completed and unfinished
jobs, exact replay, changed-input replay and invalid work.

Supply a plausible wrong repair that marks work complete before publishing its
result, or repeats publication after a restart. Explain the concrete case that
rejects it. Expected effects must follow from the documented commit rule.

## Submission

Deliver the full authoring package in the project guide, including a reference
repair, independent verification and reproduction notes. The work is the complete
task another solver can attempt, not a report describing queue design.

tasks.title: Author a verified snapshot and restore task
tasks.description:
# Author a verified directory-restore task

## Situation

A local backup utility can list a snapshot, but its restore path modifies the
current destination before it knows whether the snapshot is valid. A damaged
snapshot can leave a mixture of old and restored files. Turn this into a practical
repair task with an explicit publication boundary.

## What you create

Supply a small implementation, an original fixture directory and documented
snapshot/restore commands. Include nested directories, an empty file, a filename
with spaces and two files with the same length but different contents. The solver
should be able to demonstrate the failure using the supplied tools.

Keep the format small enough to inspect. Choose a local manifest and content
layout rather than relying on an external backup service. The task need not be a
general-purpose backup product.

## Behavior the finished task must specify

- A manifest identifies the required paths, entry types, content lengths and
  content digests. Restore checks the complete declared content.
- Invalid content, a missing object, duplicate destination paths or a path outside
  the restore root cannot produce a successful restore.
- Until publication succeeds, a failed attempt leaves the prior destination's
  content intact. Define exactly what may remain in temporary storage and how a
  later attempt handles it.
- Successful restore produces the specified tree, including empty directories
  and files. State how extra files in an existing destination are treated.
- Repeating a successful restore has a documented result and does not corrupt
  the retained snapshot.

Define which metadata is preserved; do not leave permissions, timestamps or links
implicitly graded. You may exclude unsupported entry types if the instructions
state that they are rejected. Choose and explain the publication mechanism and
supported filesystem assumptions.

## Evidence the task must support

Compare destination contents before and after rejected restores. Exercise a
corrupted object of unchanged length, a missing object and an interruption before
publication, then repeat recovery. Inspect the final tree rather than accepting a
success message. Use independent content digests and known original fixture bytes.

Include a plausible incorrect repair that validates only lengths or validates
files after overwriting the destination. Show the specific assertion that exposes
it while an ordinary restore still succeeds.

## Submission

Provide the complete package required by the project guide. Your reference and
verification must demonstrate the declared filesystem guarantees, not guarantees
that depend on an unstated platform feature.

tasks.title: Author a dependency-aware incremental build task
tasks.description:
# Author a dependency-aware incremental build task

## Situation

A team uses a small local build planner to regenerate artifacts after inputs
change. It works for a simple chain but mishandles shared prerequisites and can
record a failed build as current. Create a task where the solver repairs the
planner and proves that its produced artifacts remain trustworthy.

## What you create

Provide source for the planner, a compact graph format and deterministic local
build steps. The example graph should include a branching dependency and a shared
prerequisite. Build steps may transform small text or structured files; a large
compiler toolchain is unnecessary. Document the interface for planning, building
and inspecting retained build state.

## Behavior the finished task must specify

- Dependencies complete before their consumers. Define the deterministic order
  for independent ready nodes if order is exposed in an output contract.
- Unchanged inputs reuse valid prior output. A change to an input or a declared
  build recipe invalidates the affected node and its dependents.
- Shared prerequisites are handled once per invocation, and missing output is
  never treated as a valid cache hit.
- A failed step prevents its consumers from being published as successful. A
  later invocation can recover without accepting an incomplete artifact.
- Unknown dependencies and cycles produce a useful failure with no falsely
  completed output.

Specify how changes are identified, how input deletion is handled, and what
happens to previously valid output when a rebuild fails. The task is local; do
not require a remote cache. Parallel execution is optional and must not be an
unstated requirement.

## Evidence the task must support

Build twice with unchanged inputs, then change one branch and inspect exactly
which steps rerun and which artifact bytes change. Include a recipe change,
missing output, failed shared prerequisite, cycle and recovery after failure.
Derive expected affected nodes independently of the planner's own traversal.

Supply an incomplete repair that invalidates only direct dependents or marks a
step complete before its command succeeds. Show why a simple chain test would
miss the error and why your branching or failure case detects it.

## Submission

Deliver the full authoring package with a reference repair, verification and
resource observations. The resulting solver task must assess build correctness,
not familiarity with a particular commercial build service.

tasks.title: Author an atomic local database upgrade task
tasks.description:
# Author an atomic local database-upgrade task

## Situation

A desktop tool stores records in a local database. Its next release changes a
record representation, but the upgrade utility can update the version marker
before conversion finishes. Create a terminal task where the solver repairs the
upgrade without losing retained data.

## What you create

Provide a small utility, starting database fixtures generated from original
records, and explicit source and destination schemas. Use a local database engine
available in the declared environment. Choose a conversion with meaningful edge
cases, such as preserving exact fixed-point values while separating one field
into several columns. Avoid private or production data.

## Behavior the finished task must specify

- Every supported source version has an explicit conversion rule. Required
  identifiers and relationships are preserved.
- A successful upgrade produces the destination schema and exact converted
  values before marking that version complete.
- A conversion error or an interruption before commit leaves the prior database
  usable under its original schema and version.
- Running the upgrade again on an already upgraded database has a defined safe
  outcome without repeating a data transformation.
- An unsupported version is rejected without changing the database.

Define nullable values, range boundaries, invalid input and any numeric rounding
rule. State whether concurrent callers are supported. If only exclusive access is
supported, document how contention is reported rather than grading an unspecified
race behavior. Identify the transaction boundary in the solver-facing contract.

## Evidence the task must support

Inspect both schema and retained values after success. Exercise an intermediate
conversion failure, a controlled interruption before commit, exact replay and an
unsupported version. Compare the rejected database with its original usable state.
Expected converted values must be derived independently of the upgrade routine.

Include a wrong repair that advances the version marker separately or commits
converted rows in batches. A fixture whose error occurs after some valid rows
must detect partial application. A happy-path-only case is insufficient.

## Submission

Provide the complete task package, including the reference, verification and
reproduction notes. A design document without runnable starting and repaired
states does not fulfill this authoring assignment.

tasks.title: Author a deterministic event-correlation task
tasks.description:
# Author a deterministic event-correlation task

## Situation

A support tool combines locally exported event streams into operation summaries.
Repeated delivery, shuffled records and equal timestamps expose defects that do
not appear in a neatly ordered sample. Create a task where the solver repairs the
correlation logic and its observable outputs.

## What you create

Supply a small command-line program, original event fixtures and a documented
input/output format. Use realistic but fictional operation identifiers. Include
a visible example that explains the output without revealing every verification
case. The task must run locally without a logging provider or external account.

## Behavior the finished task must specify

- Event identity determines whether a record is an exact duplicate. Define what
  happens when the same identity appears with conflicting content.
- Timestamp parsing, timezone normalization and tie-breaking are explicit.
  Equal timestamps must actually occur in the supplied verification cases.
- The output contains the required per-operation state and values. Define how
  missing events, unknown event types and malformed records are handled.
- Reordering input records within the documented equivalence rules does not
  change the meaning of the output. Define any output ordering requirement.
- One operation's invalid event cannot silently change another operation's
  summary. State whether the tool rejects a whole input or reports partial
  results, including the corresponding exit status.

Choose a bounded event model and specify it completely. Do not assume that start
and finish events always arrive in timestamp order. Explain exactly how durations
or other computed values are derived, including invalid or incomplete pairs.

## Evidence the task must support

Use duplicate records, conflicting duplicates, timezone-equivalent timestamps,
ties, missing records and shuffled input. Compare parsed output fields with
independently worked expected values. Test the documented error policy and exit
status; counting output rows alone is not sufficient.

Provide a plausible repair that sorts only by timestamp or discards every repeated
identity without checking its content. Show the input where this repair produces
a convincing but incorrect summary.

## Submission

Deliver the full package required by the project guide. The goal is a clear,
reproducible solver challenge, not a fixed-output exercise that can pass by
memorizing the visible sample.
